assessments.reasoning: The survey instrument allows distinguishing de jure versus de facto female-headed households because it collects individual sex (Capítulo E, Q3), relationship to household head (Capítulo E, Q5), marital status (Capítulo E, Q11), co-residence of spouse (Capítulo E, Q12), and remittance income from persons outside the household (Capítulo L, Q4). Unpartnered mother-child units can be uniquely identified within any household because Q5A and Q5B record the specific line numbers for mother and father residing in the household, alongside marital and co-resident partner status (Q11, Q12). Women-maintained households or units can be identified through individual income variables collected for all individuals aged 10 and older (Capítulo I, Q17, Q48; Capítulo L), enabling the identification of the primary provider regardless of who is designated as the reference person in Q5. However, the instrument does not link mother-child sub-units to their own separate consumption, production, or care activity (hearth-hold proxy), as household facilities and food preparation are collected strictly at the overall household level (Capítulo C), and care activities in Capítulo K are referenced to 'Su hogar' as a whole rather than disaggregated by mother-child sub-units.
